title: Ultra Hello World
content:
This example demonstrates the absolute minimal footprint of Gravito, showcasing the simplest possible route implementation. Perfect for understanding the core concepts before diving into more complex features.

Standalone Photon (Minimal)

The simplest way to create a route using Photon directly:

import { Photon } from '@gravito/photon'

const app = new Photon()

// Simple GET route
app.get('/hello', (c) => {
  return c.text('Hello, World!')
})

// JSON response
app.get('/api/hello', (c) => {
  return c.json({ message: 'Hello, World!' })
})

// Start server
Bun.serve({
  port: 3000,
  fetch: app.fetch
})

console.log('🚀 Server running at http://localhost:3000')

With PlanetCore (Full Framework)

Using PlanetCore for a complete application setup:

import { PlanetCore, defineConfig } from '@gravito/core'
import { BunNativeAdapter } from '@gravito/core'

const config = defineConfig({
  adapter: new BunNativeAdapter(),
  config: {
    APP_NAME: 'Hello World App',
    PORT: 3000
  }
})

async function main() {
  const core = await PlanetCore.boot(config)
  
  // Register routes
  core.router.get('/', (c) => {
    return c.json({ message: 'Hello, World!' })
  })
  
  core.router.get('/hello/:name', (c) => {
    const name = c.req.param('name')
    return c.text(`Hello, ${name}!`)
  })
  
  // Start server
  const liftoff = core.liftoff()
  Bun.serve(liftoff)
  console.log(`🚀 App running at http://localhost:${liftoff.port}`)
}

main().catch(console.error)

Response Types

Gravito supports multiple response types:

app.get('/text', (c) => c.text('Plain text response'))
app.get('/json', (c) => c.json({ data: 'JSON response' }))
app.get('/html', (c) => c.html('
HTML Response
'))
app.get('/redirect', (c) => c.redirect('/hello'))
app.get('/status', (c) => c.json({ ok: true }, 201))

Route Parameters

Access dynamic route parameters:

// Single parameter
app.get('/users/:id', (c) => {
  const id = c.req.param('id')
  return c.json({ userId: id })
})

// Multiple parameters
app.get('/posts/:postId/comments/:commentId', (c) => {
  const postId = c.req.param('postId')
  const commentId = c.req.param('commentId')
  return c.json({ postId, commentId })
})

// Query parameters
app.get('/search', (c) => {
  const query = c.req.query('q')
  const page = c.req.query('page') || '1'
  return c.json({ query, page })
})

Request Body

Handle POST requests with JSON data:

app.post('/users', async (c) => {
  const body = await c.req.json()
  return c.json({ created: body }, 201)
})

// Form data
app.post('/form', async (c) => {
  const form = await c.req.formData()
  const name = form.get('name')
  return c.json({ name })
})

Middleware

Add middleware for logging, authentication, etc.:

// Global middleware
app.use(async (c, next) => {
  console.log(`${c.req.method} ${c.req.path}`)
  await next()
})

// Path-specific middleware
app.use('/api/*', async (c, next) => {
  c.header('X-API-Version', '1.0')
  await next()
})

// Route with middleware
app.get('/api/data', async (c, next) => {
  // Before handler
  console.log('Before')
  await next()
  // After handler
  console.log('After')
}, (c) => {
  return c.json({ data: 'response' })
})

Error Handling

Handle errors gracefully:

// Global error handler
app.onError((err, c) => {
  console.error('Error:', err)
  return c.json({ error: err.message }, 500)
})

// 404 handler
app.notFound((c) => {
  return c.json({ error: 'Not found' }, 404)
})

// Try-catch in route
app.get('/risky', async (c) => {
  try {
    // Risky operation
    return c.json({ success: true })
  } catch (err) {
    return c.json({ error: 'Something went wrong' }, 500)
  }
})

Complete Example

Here's a complete, runnable example:

import { Photon } from '@gravito/photon'

const app = new Photon()

// Middleware
app.use(async (c, next) => {
  console.log(`[${new Date().toISOString()}] ${c.req.method} ${c.req.path}`)
  await next()
})

// Routes
app.get('/', (c) => c.json({ message: 'Hello, World!' }))

app.get('/hello/:name', (c) => {
  const name = c.req.param('name')
  return c.text(`Hello, ${name}!`)
})

app.post('/echo', async (c) => {
  const body = await c.req.json()
  return c.json({ echo: body })
})

// Error handling
app.onError((err, c) => {
  return c.json({ error: err.message }, 500)
})

app.notFound((c) => {
  return c.json({ error: 'Not found' }, 404)
})

// Start server
const server = Bun.serve({
  port: 3000,
  fetch: app.fetch
})

console.log(`🚀 Server running at http://localhost:${server.port}`)
console.log('\nTry these routes:')
console.log('  GET  http://localhost:3000/')
console.log('  GET  http://localhost:3000/hello/Gravito')
console.log('  POST http://localhost:3000/echo')

Running the Example

Save the code to index.ts and run:

bun run index.ts

Or use the Bun runtime directly:

bun index.ts

Next Steps

  • Add more routes and explore routing patterns
  • Integrate with a database using @gravito/atlas
  • Add authentication with @gravito/sentinel
  • Build a full-stack app with @gravito/ion

Performance: This minimal example demonstrates Gravito's zero-overhead design. Even with middleware and error handling, the performance remains excellent thanks to Bun's native runtime.
